part.text: Done. I rewrote `markdown.go` as a clean line-based renderer; all 17 test cases pass and `go vet` is clean. No other files were touched. **What changed** (the original scanned the document one character at a time with five intertwined pieces of state: `header`, `he`, `list`, `listOpened`, and a manual `pos` cursor): - **`Render`** now splits the input into lines and renders each one as exactly one of three things — a header, a list item, or paragraph text — with a single `inList` boolean as the only state. - **`parseHeader`** extracts the header level and text from a line's leading `#` run. The 7-hash special case (rendered as a literal paragraph) is handled explicitly at the call site instead of via the `header == 7` / `he` flag tricks. - **`closeList`** centralizes emitting `` when a list ends (before a header, before a paragraph, or at end of document). - **`applyEmphasis` / `wrapFirstPair`** replace the four chained `strings.Replace` calls with one helper that wraps the first pair of `__` or `_` markers. It also fixes a latent bug: the original would emit an unclosed ``/`` if a marker appeared only once, while the new code leaves unpaired markers alone. - **`strings.Builder`** replaces repeated `html += ...` string concatenation. The refactoring notes are captured in comments, as the spec suggests. A couple of untested edge cases now behave more sanely than the original (e.g., a lone `*` mid-line is literal text, and a line of just `#` no longer panics with an index-out-of-range).
